title: Research Methodology: Definition, Nature and Characteristics
summary: Meaning of research; scientific, controlled, empirical and critical characteristics; quantitative vs qualitative research; research as science, social science, applied science and dynamic discipline.
objectives: Define research and state its four characteristics.
Explain research as science, social science, applied science and dynamic discipline.
revision: Research = systematic, controlled, empirical, critical investigation. Quantitative tests hypotheses; qualitative explores meanings.
traps: Kerlinger's definition is often quoted verbatim; memorise 'systematic, controlled, empirical and critical'.
Research is not the same as information gathering.
confusions: Confusing quantitative research with qualitative research.
Believing research must always be experimental.

notes.t: Research is a systematic, controlled, empirical and critical investigation of hypothetical propositions about the presumed relations among natural phenomena (Fred N. Kerlinger). It is a systematic and organized process of investigating a problem, gathering data, analysing information and drawing conclusions to expand knowledge or solve real-world issues.
A systematic, controlled, empirical and critical investigation of hypothetical propositions about the presumed relations among natural phenomena.

i: Systematic — follows a planned, step-by-step procedure.
Controlled — variables are controlled to understand cause-and-effect relationships.
Empirical — based on observation and experimentation rather than theory alone.
Critical — involves careful and exacting investigation.

notes.t: Nature of psychology research as a discipline

Research methodology in psychology is best understood as several things at once: a science (systematic, empirical methods; testable and falsifiable hypotheses), a social science (people in social and cultural contexts), an applied science (findings applied to clinical, educational, organisational problems) and a dynamic discipline (methods evolve as the field matures).

Research is systematic, controlled, empirical and critical. Kerlinger's definition is frequently cited in UGC NET. Quantitative research tests hypotheses; qualitative research explores deeper insights.
